abstract_predicate_verification.argument: If no nonminor precedes a later minor, all prior minor content lies before nonminor content. Removing excluded tokens cannot introduce an inversion, so the first n_minor eligible positions are exactly the aligned minor mask. If an inversion exists, masks can differ, but empty/excluded spans can remove it.

design_consequences: Only2.48percent is even structurally capable of distinguishing the current aligned and count-matched chronological prior masks; actual token exclusions can reduce this upper bound.
The possible rows are concentrated in a few source groups, not broad evidence for role-attribution generalization. Existing TRAIN/DEV alone is a weak mechanism-discriminating design.

Identical input masks/features do not imply identical predictions from separately trained models: parameter updates on differing rows can change outputs elsewhere. Therefore global improvement alone cannot prove a broad alignment mechanism.
